what_it_does: This paper describes a high-density NAND Flash memory chip (the technology behind SSDs and USB drives) with 321 layers of cells stacked vertically, achieving 2 terabits of storage. Each cell stores 4 bits of data (four times more than earlier single-bit designs), and the chip achieves a fast 75 megabytes per second program (write) throughput. This combination of extreme density, storage capacity per cell, and write speed makes it suitable for enterprise data centers and AI workloads that demand rapid data movement while maintaining reliability.
